items.title: Definition 16.1.1 (2017: 16.1), polyfold structures

book.label: §16.1, Definition 16.1.1, p. 705 (2017: Definition 16.1)
book.statement: A polyfold structure on a space $Z$ is a pair $(X, \beta)$: an ep-groupoid $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact satisfying (ZHOU), and a homeomorphism $\beta : |X| \to Z$.

lean.statement: `structure PolyfoldStructure (Z)`, with fields `X`, `paracompact : X.X.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`, `isZhou : X.X.IsZhou` and `β : X.X.OrbitSpace ≃ₜ Z`; `toOrbitChart` (the pair of Remark 10.3.18) and `isLR`. Witness: `z3PolyfoldStructure` on $\mathbb R$ (the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action).

diff: $Z$ lives in the universe of the object and morphism sets of $X$. The text's remark that $Z$ is then metrizable is gap G.146. The 2017 definition had neither (ZHOU) nor paracompactness.

book.label: §16.1, Definition 16.1.2, p. 707 (2017: Definition 16.2)
book.statement: $(X, \alpha) \sim (Y, \beta)$ if there is a generalized isomorphism $f : X \to Y$ with $\alpha = \beta \circ |f|$.

lean.statement: `PolyfoldStructure.Equiv p q := ∃ f, IsGeneralizedIso f ∧ ⇑p.β = ⇑q.β ∘ orbitMap f`; an equivalence relation (`setoid`), equal to Remark 10.3.18's relation (`equiv_iff_rel`); $|f| = \beta^{-1} \circ \alpha$ (`orbitMap_eq_of_equiv`).

items.title: The uniqueness sentence after Definition 16.1.2

book.label: §16.1, after Definition 16.1.2, p. 707 (2017: Definition 16.2)
book.statement: The generalized isomorphism $f$ with $\alpha = \beta \circ |f|$ is unique, as a consequence of (ZHOU) (through Theorem 10.3.19).

lean.statement: Does not hold as we read it: `PolyfoldStructure.not_uniqueness_16_1_2 : ¬ Uniqueness_16_1_2`. The trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-ep-groupoid on $\mathbb R$ satisfies (ZHOU) (`isZhou_trivialZ3`) and has paracompact orbit space, so it is a polyfold structure on $\mathbb R$ in the sense of Definition 16.1.1; the identity and the generalized isomorphism through the inversion functor both satisfy $\alpha = \alpha \circ |f|$ and differ (`uniqueness_16_1_2_counterexample`). It holds when the target is effective: `uniqueness_16_1_2_of_isEffective` ((ZHOU) gives the local regularity property, then Theorem 10.3.19 for effective ep-groupoids).

chips: does not hold as we read it
diff: The sentence does not hold as we read it (Findings, Chapter 16, item 1): the counterexample satisfies every printed hypothesis, (ZHOU), paracompact $|X|$ and $\beta$ a homeomorphism, all proved for the instance. It is the pair behind `not_theorem_10_3_19` (Chapter 10). The effective form is proved. The 2017 text (Definition 16.2) says "$f$ is necessarily unique", citing the theorem that is now 10.3.19; the 2021 text adds "as a consequence of (ZHOU)".

items.title: Definition 16.1.3 (2017: 16.3), polyfolds

book.label: §16.1, Definition 16.1.3, p. 707 (2017: Definition 16.3)
book.statement: A polyfold is a pair $(Z, c)$, $c$ an equivalence class of polyfold structures on $Z$.

diff: A class is a Lean quotient; the book's footnote on classes does not arise.

items.title: Proposition 16.1.4 (2017: 16.2), bump functions and partitions of unity are invariant

book.label: §16.1, Proposition 16.1.4, p. 708 (2017: Proposition 16.2)
book.statement: For equivalent $(X, \alpha)$, $(Y, \beta)$: (1) $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions iff $Y$ does; (2) $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity iff $Y$ does.

lean.statement: `PolyfoldStructure.proposition_16_1_4`: `(p.X.X.PObj.AdmitsBumpFunctions ↔ q.X.X.PObj.AdmitsBumpFunctions) ∧ (p.X.X.HasScPartitionsOfUnity ↔ q.X.X.HasScPartitionsOfUnity)`; parts `proposition_16_1_4_one`, `_two`, through equivalences (`IsEquivalence.admitsBumpFunctions_iff`, `IsEquivalence.hasScPartitionsOfUnity_iff`); the "easy exercise" is `isScSmoothMap_comp_π_of_comp_obj`.

diff: (1) is read for the object M-polyfold (Definition 5.3.1, $f(x) \ne 0$), as the proof uses it; Definition 12.3.1's notion is equivalent by Theorem 12.3.2 (1) (V12.11). (2) is Definition 7.5.5. The proof route differs: local inverses for (1), partitions descended to $|X|$ for (2).

items.title: Definition 16.1.5 (2017: 16.4), polyfolds with bump functions and partitions of unity

book.label: §16.1, Definition 16.1.5, p. 708 (2017: Definition 16.4)
book.statement: $(Z, c)$ admits sc-smooth bump functions (partitions of unity) if some $(X, \alpha) \in c$ does; then all do.

lean.statement: `PolyfoldClass.AdmitsBumpFunctions`, `PolyfoldClass.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity` (some structure in $c$); `definition_16_1_5_one`, `_two`: equivalent to "every structure in $c$". Witnesses `z3Polyfold_admitsBumpFunctions`, `z3Polyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity`.

diff: Bump functions with the object M-polyfold reading, as in V16.5.

items.title: Remark 16.1.7 (2017: 16.1), at most one generalized isomorphism over a homeomorphism

book.label: §16.1, Remark 16.1.7, p. 711 (2017: Remark 16.1), and pp. 709–710
book.statement: For a homeomorphism $h : Z \to W$ there is at most one generalized isomorphism $f$ with $h \circ \alpha = \beta \circ |f|$; for continuous $h$ there may be none or many. (Also pp. 709–710: for isomorphisms of polyfold structures, the generalized isomorphism is determined by the map, as a consequence of Theorem 10.3.19.)

lean.statement: Does not hold as we read it: `PolyfoldStructure.not_remark_16_1_7 : ¬ Remark_16_1_7` (the pair of V16.3, $h = \mathrm{id}$); the same pair contradicts the sentence on pp. 709–710. Holds for an effective target: `remark_16_1_7_of_isEffective`.

chips: does not hold as we read it
diff: Does not hold as we read it (Findings, Chapter 16, item 2); the effective form is proved. The "none or many" sentence for continuous $h$ has no content beyond an example and is not formalized.

items.title: Lemma 16.1.13 (2017: 16.1), the degeneracy index does not depend on the structure

book.label: §16.1, Lemma 16.1.13, p. 712 (2017: Lemma 16.1)
book.statement: Equivalent structures give $d_{(X,\beta)} = d_{(X',\beta')}$, where $d_{(X,\beta)}(z) = d_X(x)$ for $\beta(|x|) = z$.

lean.statement: `PolyfoldStructure.degIndex p z := d_{|X|}(β⁻¹ z)`, equal to $d_X(x)$ for every $x$ with $\beta(|x|) = z$ (`degIndex_eq`); `lemma_16_1_13 (h : Equiv p q) : p.degIndex = q.degIndex`.

items.title: Definition 16.1.14 (2017: 16.9), the degeneracy index of a polyfold

book.label: §16.1, Definition 16.1.14, p. 712 (2017: Definition 16.9)
book.statement: $d_Z : Z \to \mathbb N$ with $d_Z(z) = d_X(x)$ for every $(X, \beta) \in c$ and $\beta(|x|) = z$.

lean.statement: `PolyfoldClass.degIndex c` (`Quotient.lift`); `definition_16_1_14`: `c.degIndex z = d_X(x)` for every representative and every $x$ over $z$. Witness `z3Polyfold_degIndex`.

items.title: Definition 16.1.17 (2017: 16.11), the boundary of a polyfold

lean.statement: `PolyfoldClass.boundary c := {z | 1 ≤ c.degIndex z}`; `mem_boundary_iff` (through any representative). Witness `z3Polyfold_boundary` ($= \emptyset$).

book.label: §16.1, Lemma 16.1.19, p. 714 (2017: Lemma 16.2)
book.statement: If $(X, \alpha) \sim (Y, \beta)$ and $X$ is tame, so is $Y$.

book.label: §16.1, Definition 16.1.20, p. 714 (2017: Definition 16.12)
book.statement: $(Z, c)$ is tame if one (then every) $(X, \beta) \in c$ has $X$ tame.

lean.statement: `PolyfoldClass.IsTame c := ∃ p, ⟦p⟧ = c ∧ p.X.X.IsTame`; `definition_16_1_20`: equivalent to every representative tame. Witness `z3Polyfold_isTame`.

items.title: The polyfold $\mathbb R$ with nontrivial isotropy (witness)

lean.statement: The trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-ep-groupoid on $\mathbb R$: $\pi$ is injective and a homeomorphism onto $\mathbb R$ (`injective_π_trivialZ3`, `isHomeomorph_π_trivialZ3`, `trivialZ3OrbitHomeomorph`), with paracompact orbit space (`hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivialZ3`); tools `PartitionOfUnity.comapP3Z`, `EpGroupoid.descendP3Z`, `preimage_closure_π`, `MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_real_of_locally`.

notFormalized.title: Polyfolds are metrizable (the remark after Definition 16.1.1)
notFormalized.label: §16.1, after Definition 16.1.1, p. 706 (2017: Proposition 16.1)
notFormalized.book: If $|X|$ is paracompact, $Z \cong |X|$ is metrizable (locally metrizable, regular, Hausdorff and paracompact: Nagata–Smirnov).
notFormalized.instead: Local metrizability of $|X|$ (`lemma_7_3_2_naturalRep`), regularity and the Hausdorff property (Lemmas 7.3.4, 7.3.5) exist; the Smirnov metrization theorem is not in Mathlib (estimate 600–1,500 lines). In 2017 this was the numbered Proposition 16.1; in the 2021 text it is a remark in prose.
